events.name: The Frozen Cavern
events.intro: A crack in the glacier breathes cold, blue light. From deep inside comes a small, steady sound: tick, tick, tick. Something in there is working ice with a tool.

success.text: The ice closes overhead. On the wall beside the entrance, at knee height, someone has carved a perfect little Rattata. It is looking at you.
You pull your collar up and go round the glacier. The ticking goes on behind you, patient, a hundred carvings from finished.

events.name: Frozen Cavern
events.intro: Blue light comes down through ice as thick as a house. A Snover shuffles out of a drift, shakes snow off its head like a dog, and holds one mitten out to you.

success.text: It takes back the mitten and puts up both.
Its mitten is cold and very solemn. It shakes twice, as it has seen people do, then presses a perfectly round Snowball into your palm: a gift, packed with great care.
You nod and walk past. It keeps its mitten out a moment longer, then tucks it away.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Frozen Cavern will wait.

events.name: Frozen Cavern: trap
events.intro: The tunnel crosses a frozen pool. The ice is thin and grey in the middle, scuffed at the edge where others stood, thought about it, and turned back.

success.text: You push off and glide across in one breath, arms out, the ice singing under you. You arrive laughing.

failure.text: Halfway over, the ice goes off like a gunshot. Everyone scrambles out the far side, soaked to the waist and shaking.

success.text: Your Ice-type walks out, breathes on the grey ice until it goes white and hard, and beckons you over a floor it made itself.
You take the long gallery round the pool, an hour of squeezing sideways through blue cracks. Slow, cold, and perfectly safe.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Frozen Cavern will wait.

events.name: Frozen Cavern: rest
events.intro: A dry corner out of the wind. All around it the walls are carved: a Pikachu mid-leap, a Snorlax asleep, a Lapras with every shell-stud in place. They are extraordinarily good. They are all at eye level for something tall.

success.text: You sleep among the carvings. It is like sleeping in a crowd of friends holding very still.

You walk the wall slowly. Near the end the ice is fresh, the chips still on the floor. It is your starter. Not the species: yours, with the look it gets before a battle. Something watched you come in, and carved it while you walked.

You scratch away with a tent peg for an hour. It is not good. It is recognisably a Pokémon, if you are kind. You leave it at the end of the wall, next to the masterpieces, for whoever made them to find.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Frozen Cavern will wait.

remembers.notice: Your own crooked carving stands at the end of the wall, beside your starter's.
Your starter looks back at you from the ice.
Your own crooked carving stands at the end of the wall.

events.name: Frozen Cavern: rare
events.intro: An unusual cry echoes down the tunnel. Whatever it is, it does not belong here: a Darumaka, but white as the walls, with a snowball for a nose, from another region entirely. It is shivering. It is delighted.

success.text: It rolls into the ball like a snowball downhill, giggling.

It acts it out for you. Walking. Walking. A lot of walking. Snow, more snow, a boat perhaps, then this place, colder than anywhere, and it throws its arms up: perfect. It walked in over a winter and liked it. It is a very long way from home.
You leave it rolling happily in a drift, the only one of its kind for a thousand miles, and not minding at all.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Frozen Cavern will wait.

remembers.intro: The white Darumaka sits in the snow watching you, head on one side. It came a very long way. What happens to the one far from home?

addChoices.label: Escort it to the pass. (two nodes)

success.text: You walk it out through the high tunnels toward the pass that leads home. Something has been following the smell of a small, lost thing. It steps out of the dark ahead of you.

win.text: You walked a Galarian Darumaka to the pass that leads home.

success.text: It comes with you gladly. But that night, and for many nights, it sits facing the direction it came from, quiet, before it sleeps.

You sit down and wait. It looks at you. It looks at the perfect cold. It pats your boot, kindly, as you would pat someone who cannot help not being a glacier, and rolls back into its drift. It has decided.

events.name: Frozen Cavern: wild
events.intro: A pack of Sneasel comes skittering down the tunnel toward you with their arms full of small bright tools: ice chisels, a dozen of them, stolen. Behind them, far off, a deep unhappy roar.

success.text: They drop into a ring around you, chisels clutched tight.
You go after them over the ice, cut them off at a bend, and they scatter in a clatter of dropped steel. A dozen fine chisels, each handle worn by a huge paw. Whoever owns these will want them.

failure.text: You slip at the bend and they turn on you, laughing. You will have to take the chisels the hard way.

success.text: You flatten against the wall and they pour past, cackling. The roar behind them sounds less angry than heartbroken.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Frozen Cavern will wait.

events.name: Frozen Cavern: den
events.intro: Claw marks and nests line the walls. This is somebody's home. An Alpha Mamoswine fills the cave, frost thick on its tusks, eyes red. Tucked against its side, half under the fur: a calf, small, shivering, too cold even for here.

choices.label: Calm it with a Never-Melt Ice.

success.text: You set the Never-Melt Ice on the floor between you. The Mamoswine snuffs it, crunches it, and lets out a long breath that fogs the whole cave. The red fades. It turns its great head back to the calf, and lets you by.
It puts itself between you and the calf, and charges.

Your Fire-type walks forward slowly, sits down by the calf, and simply glows. The shivering stops. The calf sighs and burrows against the warmth. The Mamoswine watches for a long time. Then it lies down, all at once, like a hill settling.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Frozen Cavern will wait.

events.name: Frozen Cavern: boss
events.intro: The deepest room: a hall of ice, and the Beartic, carving. The whole wall is Pokémon, a hundred of them, every one it has ever seen. In the middle one figure stands half finished, rough-cut: not a Pokémon. A trainer.

success.text: You stand still. The Beartic looks at you, looks at the ice, and works. Chips fly for an hour. When it steps back, the trainer in the wall has your coat, your stance, your face. In a hundred carvings of Pokémon it left one space for a person, and waited to see who would come.

effects.text: The Ice Sculptor carved you into its wall.

success.text: It drops the chisel and rises on its hind legs in front of the wall. Not one carving will be touched.

You hold out the stolen chisels. The Beartic counts them with one claw, twice. Then it bows, very low. It breaks a block from the wall and carves, fast and sure, and puts the result in your hands: your starter, small enough to carry, every line right.

effects.text: The Ice Sculptor gave you a carving of your starter.

success.text: You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Frozen Cavern will wait.

events.name: Frozen Cavern: exit
events.intro: Daylight, white and blinding after so much blue.

success.text: You turn. Sun strikes down through the glacier, and for one moment the whole carved wall lights from inside. Every Pokémon you have ever met is there, glowing. You had not counted how many. The Sculptor had.

effects.text: You saw the whole wall of the Frozen Cavern lit by the sun.

success.text: You walk out into the snow without looking back. Behind you, faintly: tick, tick, tick.

remembers.notice: Somewhere back in the blue, you are part of the wall now, standing among a hundred friends.
The little ice starter in your pack has not melted. You suspect it never will.
The ticking has stopped. You fought the Sculptor in front of its own wall, and the cavern is very quiet.

events.name: The Volcanic Core
events.intro: A vent in the mountainside glows dull red, and the rock is warm under your hand. The town at the volcano's foot says the oldest fire in the country burns in there, older than the town, and that something tends it.

success.text: The warmth wraps round you like a held breath. Far below, slow as a heartbeat, something puffs smoke.
You skirt the mountain. A thin, steady thread of smoke rises from its top, the same as every day for a thousand years.

events.name: Volcanic Core
events.intro: Warm rock, getting warmer. A Slugma slides across the path, leaving a glowing trail, and stops to stare at you with huge yellow eyes, as if it has never seen anything so cold.

success.text: It puffs itself up, dripping fire.
You step over. It watches your boot go by with deep interest.
It slides on and you follow its cooling trail. It keeps to the black rock, the old rock, away from every red seam. It has lived here always. It knows where the mountain is asleep.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Volcanic Core will wait.

events.name: Volcanic Core: trap
events.intro: The floor's wrong: a black crust, thin as pie, over something that glows through the cracks. There are scuff marks where others turned back, and one boot print that goes on, and stops.

success.text: You throw stones ahead. Where one sinks hissing, you do not step. It takes patience and every stone in reach.
Your Fire-type strolls out across the crust as if over a lawn, finds the thick places by feel, and scorches a marked path for the rest of you.
You sprint. The crust dips and cracks behind every footfall, and you make the far side with your soles smoking and nothing worse.

failure.text: You sprint. The crust breaks under your lead's last stride, and it comes out the far side scorched and wincing.

success.text: You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Volcanic Core will wait.

remembers.notice: The Slugma you followed slides out ahead of you and crosses on a line of old black rock, without a pause.

success.text: You put your feet exactly where it went. The crust on either side glows and ticks. Under you it is cold, solid, a thousand years asleep. The Slugma waits to see you over, then slides away.

events.name: Volcanic Core: cache
events.intro: A battered chest: a geologist's instrument case, lid warped by heat. A note is tucked under the strap in a hurried hand: "If found, the readings say it's waking. Tell the town."

success.text: Pages of careful numbers, climbing. You do not need to understand them to see the shape. You fold them inside your coat, next to your chest, to carry down to people who will.
Under the instruments, packed in asbestos cloth: a lump of Charcoal and a Fire Stone, samples from the deep.
You take the samples and the pages. The pages weigh nothing, and feel like the heavier of the two.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Volcanic Core will wait.

events.name: Volcanic Core: den
events.intro: Claw marks and nests line the walls. This is somebody's home. A Houndoom pack rises from the warm rock as one, and at their head an Alpha, red-eyed, horns like a crown. Behind them, in a hollow: pups, a heap of them, asleep.

choices.label: Calm it with a Rawst Berry.

success.text: You toss the Rawst Berry. The Alpha catches it out of the air, and the bitterness seems to clear its head. It looks at you properly for the first time: small, not a threat, already leaving. It sits. The pack sits.
The Alpha does not wait for the pack.

You show your hands and walk backwards, away from the hollow, keeping the whole width of the cave between you and the pups. The Alpha paces you every step. At the far tunnel it stops, and lets you go.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Volcanic Core will wait.

remembers.notice: The Alpha knows your smell: the one who backed away from the pups. It does not rise this time.

success.text: You sit down where you are and wait. The Alpha walks over, slow, and sniffs your open hands. Then it turns its back on you, which from a Houndoom is everything, and lies down across the mouth of the hollow.

events.name: Volcanic Core: rest
events.intro: A dry, warm corner. A hot spring bubbles in a basin of smooth stone, steam curling off it, the water milky blue.

success.text: You sleep beside the spring with the warmth soaking into your back.
Everyone gets in. There is splashing. There is a great deal of sighing. Your Fire-types sink to their noses and close their eyes, home at last.
You dip a hand in, shake it dry, and go on. The spring bubbles on without you.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Volcanic Core will wait.

events.name: Volcanic Core: wild
events.intro: A lava pool, and a Magmar in it up to the chest, eyes shut, bathing. It has not seen you. It is humming.

success.text: It opens one eye, furious at the interruption.
You wait. It hums the whole tune, twice. Then it climbs out, shakes off a spray of sparks, gives you a civil nod, and strolls away down a side tunnel.
You edge round the pool on the far side. The humming never falters.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Volcanic Core will wait.

events.name: Volcanic Core: rare
events.intro: An unusual cry, thin and far off. Ahead, where the heat-haze is thickest, something stands: Charmander-shaped, but you can see the rock through it. A shadow with a flame where a tail should be.

success.text: It walks ahead of you, never nearer, never further, to a wall of old soot. There it turns, looks back once, and steps through the stone. Where it stood the rock is cold. You write down everything.
You call. It turns its head. For a moment you are looked at by something that is mostly not here. Then the haze shifts, and there is only heat.
You let it be. Some things come to an old fire to be alone.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Volcanic Core will wait.

remembers.intro: An unusual cry, thin and far off. Ahead in the heat-haze stands a shape you know now: the Ghost Dragon of the Burnt Valley, the Delta Charizard, grown and translucent, come back to sit by the oldest fire.
remembers.notice: It knows you. It dips its head, the way it did in the valley.

events.name: Volcanic Core: boss
events.intro: The deepest room. An Alpha Magcargo, enormous, lies coiled round a pit where the oldest fire in the country burns low and gold. Behind it, slow and grey with age, an old Torkoal puffs a thin thread of smoke and watches you.

success.text: Your Pokémon turns from the Magcargo and breathes fire into the pit, carefully, like someone laying a log on a hearth. The old flame leaps and steadies. The Magcargo watches it burn. Its shell stops glowing white, and it settles round the fire again, content.
It rears up out of its shell, a wall of fire between you and the pit.

You bow to the old Torkoal. It considers you through its own smoke. Then it puffs twice, short. The Magcargo lowers itself and makes room. They are partners. One keeps the fire, one guards the keeper, and they have done it since before there was a town.

effects.text: The Keeper of the Embers let you stand beside the oldest fire.

success.text: You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Volcanic Core will wait.

events.name: Volcanic Core: exit
events.intro: Daylight at the crater rim. Far below, the town is lighting its lamps for evening, each one a spark that began, long ago, up here.

choices.label: Take an ember for the town.

success.text: The Torkoal lets you lift one ember from the old fire in a clay pot. You carry it down the mountain shielded in both hands. That night the town's dark shrine is lit again from the first flame, and the elders begin, at once, to argue about a festival.

effects.text: You carried an ember of the oldest fire down to the town's shrine.

choices.label: Leave the fire where it is.

success.text: You take nothing. You stand at the rim while the smoke goes up straight into a windless sky, and something vast and warm, far away, turns its attention toward a traveller who left a fire alone.
The old Torkoal has climbed to the rim behind you; it must have taken it an hour. It nudges two things toward you with its nose: a Heat Rock, and an egg, warm as fresh bread.

remembers.notice: Below, the old fire burns unguarded tonight. The Torkoal has not followed you up.
The geologist's pages are still inside your coat. The town down there should read them.

events.name: The Ember Festival
events.intro: Word has travelled faster than you. The next town along has heard of the shrine relit from the oldest fire, and has lit its own from it, lamp to lamp, down the whole valley. Tonight there is a festival, and they have saved you a place by the fire.

success.text: They feed you until you cannot move, and the children take turns guarding the flame with great seriousness. Your team sleeps in a heap in the warmth.
You light a lantern from their fire and carry it to the edge of town, where the next village's runner is waiting to take it further. The flame you carried down a mountain is still travelling.

events.name: The Deep Ocean
events.intro: Open sea, and under the boat the water goes from blue to black. Divers say there is a light down there that has shown them the way home since the first of them went down. Four breaths of air; a Water-type helps.

success.text: You fill your lungs and go over the side. Breath: 4. The light from above narrows to a column, and you follow it down.
Your Water-type takes the lead and you hold on. It finds the easy currents; the sea carries you instead of fighting you. Breath: 6.
You row on. Deep under the keel, a small light turns, waits a while, and sinks away.

events.name: Deep Ocean
events.intro: The water darkens long before the bottom. A Mantyke glides up out of the blue and circles you, once, twice, close enough to touch, curious about the clumsy thing with two legs. Breath left: {flag:delve-deep-ocean-breath}.

success.text: It banks and comes at you, playing rough.
You match its turns. It shows you something divers take years to learn: a cold current that sinks like a lift, no kicking needed. You ride it down side by side, and arrive with air to spare.
You kick on down. The Mantyke follows a little way, then peels off toward the light.
You turn for the light and kick upward, keeping everything you carry. The deep will wait.

events.name: Deep Ocean: mystery
events.intro: Something that doesn't belong. A faint light pulses ahead, and it is not a fish. It is a crack, hanging in the water itself, as if the sea were glass. Through it: a different dark, with different stars. Breath left: {flag:delve-deep-ocean-breath}.

success.text: You back off slowly and give it the whole width of the water. Whatever is on the other side does not notice you. You were never here.

You swim to the edge and look through. Something vast looks back, without eyes, and knows your shape now. You tear yourself away with your ears ringing. The world on this side feels thinner than it did.
You tie a diver's buoy line to the rock beside it, the red kind that means: danger, tell a Ranger. Someone will follow that line down, and close this.
You turn for the light and kick upward, keeping everything you carry. The deep will wait.

events.name: Deep Ocean: trap
events.intro: The seabed's wrong: soft grey silt, scuffed where other divers turned back, dimpled in the middle like a throat. A sinkhole, breathing in. Breath left: {flag:delve-deep-ocean-breath}.

success.text: You swim hard and high over the dimple. The pull catches your ankles anyway, and you fight it stroke by stroke. You get across. It costs air you wanted.
Your Water-type noses along the bottom, finds where the silt is firm, and leads you over on a line a fish would take. You never feel the pull at all.
You follow the reef the long way round the sinkhole, slow and safe along the rock. It takes far longer than you meant to spend down here.
You turn for the light and kick upward, keeping everything you carry. The deep will wait.

events.name: Deep Ocean: rare
events.intro: An unusual cry, high and frightened. A baby Wailmer, alone, far too deep, turning in circles in the dark. Its pod is singing somewhere above, and it cannot tell which way above is. Breath left: {flag:delve-deep-ocean-breath}.

success.text: You put a hand on its side and swim up with it, up, toward the singing, until it hears the direction for itself and shoots away. Above, the song changes: one voice more. You sink back down, lungs burning, glad.

effects.text: You guided a lost baby Wailmer back up to its pod.

success.text: It comes to the ball as to the first warm thing it has met down here.
You swim on down. Behind you the small voice goes on calling, and the big voices go on answering, and neither can find the other.
You turn for the light and kick upward, keeping everything you carry. The deep will wait.

events.name: Deep Ocean: rest
events.intro: A dry corner, of all things: an air pocket trapped under the hull of a sunken ship. You come up into it gasping. The air is stale and a hundred years old, and it is the best you have ever breathed. Breath left: {flag:delve-deep-ocean-breath}.

success.text: You hang on a beam and breathe until your heart slows. The team does the same. When you are ready, your lungs are full again.
You feel along the ribs of the ship. In a rotted locker, under a captain's cap: a Big Pearl, grown fat in the dark.
You take one last breath of old air and duck back under, into the dark.
You turn for the light and kick upward, keeping everything you carry. The deep will wait.

remembers.notice: The pocket of old air waits, a little smaller for your breathing.
Your lungs are full again.
The captain's locker hangs open.

events.name: Deep Ocean: wild
events.intro: A light ahead in the black: soft, gold, steady. An old Lanturn. And round it, in tightening rings, the grey shape of a Sharpedo. Breath left: {flag:delve-deep-ocean-breath}.

success.text: You put yourself between the teeth and the light.
The Lanturn slips the Sharpedo with an old diver's trick, down through a gap in the reef, and you go after its glow. It lights your way a while. Then it is gone ahead, about its rounds.
You press into the weed until the grey shape loses interest and slides off. When you look again, the light has gone too.
You turn for the light and kick upward, keeping everything you carry. The deep will wait.

events.name: Deep Ocean: hidden
events.intro: A sealed chamber in the living reef, its lock cold and old: a carving of a Relicanth, every scale cut by hand, with a hollow where the real thing would rest. Breath left: {flag:delve-deep-ocean-breath}.

success.text: Your Relicanth swims to the carving and settles into the hollow as if returning to a chair. The reef grinds open. Inside, something kept for whoever the old fish trusted; and far below, for a moment, the whole sea seems to turn over in its sleep.
You heave at coral that was old when the ship above was built. You bruise your hands, and do not so much as stir the silt.
You leave the stone fish waiting for a real one.
You turn for the light and kick upward, keeping everything you carry. The deep will wait.

events.name: Deep Ocean: boss
events.intro: The deepest room. An Alpha Gyarados lies in the dark, curled three times round a wreck, eyes like red lamps. Every diver who came for that ship came back up without it, or did not come back up. Breath left: {flag:delve-deep-ocean-breath}.

choices.label: Calm it with the Lanturn's light.

success.text: The old Lanturn swims past you, straight to the great head, and hangs there glowing, small and gold and unafraid. The red eyes follow the light. Slow. Slower. They close. The Gyarados sleeps, as it has not slept in years. You lift the wreck's chest out from under one coil, and it does not stir.
It uncoils, and the whole wreck groans.
You look at the red eyes, and the red eyes look at you, and you go up. There is no shame in it. Everyone who is still alive made the same choice.
You turn for the light and kick upward, keeping everything you carry. The deep will wait.

remembers.notice: You know that scarred jaw, or its father's. You have met this fury before, at the lake.

events.name: Deep Ocean: exit
events.intro: The surface. Daylight, and air, endless air. The old Lanturn bobs up beside the boat, its light pale in the sun, and looks at you with one round eye.

success.text: You thank it, out loud, like a person. It flicks water at you with its tail, pleased, and waits to see what you will do next.

It thinks about it for as long as a wave takes to pass. Then it swims into your hands. It is old, and slow, and it has lit the way for strangers all its life; it would like, for once, to see where one of them goes.

effects.text: The Lantern Fish of the Deep Ocean came up into the sun with you.

success.text: It turns and sinks, its light going gold again as the water darkens round it, down and down, to wait for the next diver who needs showing home.

remembers.notice: It put a Gyarados to sleep for you with nothing but its own small light. It looks rather pleased with itself.
You put yourself between it and a Sharpedo, down there. It has not forgotten.
It watched you fight the Gyarados in the dark, and lit the way up for you anyway.

events.name: The Overgrown Forest
events.intro: The old road runs straight into a forest and does not come out. Roots have lifted the paving. Deep among the trunks you can make out straight lines that are not trees: a chimney, a gatepost, a weathervane.

success.text: The trees stand in rows, like streets. You are walking down the middle of a town.
You turn aside. The forest keeps what it is keeping.

events.name: Overgrown Forest
events.intro: Roots have swallowed the road. In a hollow stump a Phantump sits watching you with dark, round, shy eyes, as a child watches a visitor from the stairs.

success.text: It rises out of the stump, hands up, more frightened than fierce.
You wave. After a long moment a small wooden hand waves back. When you walk on, it floats after you at a careful distance, as if it has not had anyone to follow in a long time.
You walk on. The dark eyes watch you all the way to the bend.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Overgrown Forest will wait.

events.name: Overgrown Forest: den
events.intro: Claw marks and nests line the walls of what was once a front room. An Alpha Beedrill hangs in the doorway of an old house, red-eyed, guarding a hive that fills the place from floor to ceiling.

success.text: You set the Honey on the step and back away. The Alpha tastes it, and the hum of the whole hive drops a tone. It moves aside from the door. Inside, between the combs, a wall still stands; and on it, under glass, a photograph. A family. Five of them, squinting into the sun, outside this house.
It comes through the doorway like a thrown spear.
You step backwards out through the door you should not have opened, and close what is left of it. The humming settles. It is their house now.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Overgrown Forest will wait.

events.name: Overgrown Forest: puzzle
events.intro: A carved mechanism blocks the way, worn but readable: the old town gate, and on it a lock shaped like a leaf, with four smaller leaves that turn on pins.

choices.label: Turn the leaves to match the season.

success.text: You look up at the canopy, then at the lock, and turn each little leaf to match the ones overhead. The gate thinks about it. Then, with a sigh of roots, it opens.

failure.text: You turn them one way, then another. The pins click back. The trees above you stir, as if trying to give you a hint.

success.text: You put your shoulder to it. A hundred years of roots hold it shut with no effort at all.

The Phantump floats up to the lock. Its small hands turn the four leaves without looking, the way you would open your own front door. The gate swings wide. It hovers there, and will come no further. This was as far as it was ever allowed.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Overgrown Forest will wait.

events.name: Overgrown Forest: mystery
events.intro: A faint light pulses between the trunks: green, flickering, gone the instant you look straight at it. The air smells of rain from some other year.

success.text: You stand perfectly still and look at nothing. The green light comes closer. It circles you once, slowly, at the edge of your eye, the way you might walk round a statue. You feel weighed, and not found wanting. Then it is elsewhere.
You go after it. It is always one tree further. It leads you nowhere, patiently, and leaves you where you began.
You call. The light goes out like a blown candle. A while later, further off, it comes back, more careful.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Overgrown Forest will wait.

events.name: Overgrown Forest: wild
events.intro: The old town square. A crowd of Tangela has taken it over, rolling and tumbling, tangling everything: a bench, a pump, a tall stone thing in the middle wound so thick with vine you cannot tell what it was.

success.text: Half the square unrolls toward you.

You work the vines off the tall stone, strand by strand. Under them: a soldier, bare-headed, looking down. And under the soldier, cut in rows, names. Dozens of names, every one filled with moss. You clean out the first few with your thumbnail before you understand how long it would take.
You pick your way round the edge of the square. The Tangela roll on, tangling, forgetting.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Overgrown Forest will wait.

events.name: Overgrown Forest: rest
events.intro: A dry corner in an old school. Rows of small desks under ivy. A blackboard, still up, still written on in a round, firm hand.

success.text: You sleep at the teacher's desk with your head on your arms.
You rub away the grime with your sleeve. "SEE YOU AFTER THE HOLIDAY." Underneath, smaller, in a child's chalk: "see you miss."

You find the cloth, stiff as a board itself, and wipe the dust from round the words without touching one letter. At the window, a green light watches you do it, and stays a long moment before it goes.
You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Overgrown Forest will wait.

remembers.notice: The words on the board stand clear in a clean frame of slate.
"SEE YOU AFTER THE HOLIDAY."
The board is clean round its words.

events.name: Overgrown Forest: boss
events.intro: The deepest room: the town hall. An Alpha Tangrowth sits on the steps, vast, red-eyed, its vines grown through every window and out of the roof. It is not guarding the hall. It is holding it shut.

choices.label: Calm it: a Grass move at the roots, gently.

success.text: Your Pokémon does not strike. It grows: a slow green push at the Tangrowth's roots, like a hand on a shoulder. The great tangle shivers. One by one the vines let go of the window frames. The red goes out of its eyes like a lamp turned down.
It rises off the steps and the whole building creaks with it.

choices.label: Read the names on the memorial to it.

success.text: You stand at the foot of the steps and say the names you cleaned from the stone, one after another. The Tangrowth goes still. It listens to every one. When you run out of names it lowers its vines to the ground, all of them, slowly. It grew over this town so the names could stop hurting. It had not thought anyone would say them kindly.

effects.text: You read the war memorial's names to the Tangrowth that buried them.

success.text: You keep everything you carry and walk back out. The Overgrown Forest will wait.

events.name: Overgrown Forest: exit
events.intro: Daylight. The forest stands behind you, quiet, the old road running into it and not coming out.

success.text: You tell them. By the next season there are historians in the square with brushes and notebooks, cleaning moss out of names. The war is remembered. Some of the old people in the nearest town cry, and some will not speak to you.

effects.text: You told the world about the town under the Overgrown Forest.

success.text: You say nothing to anyone. As you walk away a green light keeps pace with you between the trunks, to the very last tree, and stops there. It seems, as far as a light can, to bow.

choices.label: Plant a tree at the gate.

success.text: You dig a hole in the middle of the old road and plant a sapling there. By the time you have shouldered your pack and looked back, you cannot tell which tree was yours. The forest has taken it in, and the gate is never found again.

effects.text: You planted a tree across the road to the Overgrown Forest.

remembers.notice: Somewhere back there, a Tangrowth is sitting on the town hall steps with its vines laid down, turning names over.
The town hall stands open behind you now, its keeper beaten. The forest feels thinner for it.
